Subject: Request: Updated subprocessor roster + AWS region change impact

Hi Laura,

MediSys is updating our vendor inventory and cloud continuity planning ahead of our FY27 audit. Two asks from procurement/security:

1) Can you send the most recent subprocessor/vendor roster for Redwood (including subcontracted cloud partners, monitoring/observability vendors, and any managed service providers)?
2) We received a notice that AWS intends to deprecate an older EU region (eu-central-legacy) later this year. Do you have an impact assessment or migration plan that explains how Redwood will preserve EU data residency and failover behavior for hosted and private deployments if a region is removed? Specifically: routing/fallback policies, customer-managed VPCs, and any changes to Dedicated capacity.

We'd like a short written response + any attachments you can share by EOD 2026-07-22 to include with our RFP binder.

Thanks,
Oliver
Oliver Grant
Head of Procurement
MediSys Health

Hi Oliver —

Thanks for the heads up and the deadline. High level answers below; attaching an updated subprocessor roster (redwood_subprocessor_list_2026_v2.xlsx) and a short impact note we drafted for customers.

- Subprocessors: attached spreadsheet includes cloud providers, managed monitoring, telemetry/analytics vendors, SSO/KMS partners, and support vendors. We flag which subprocessors access production data and which have SOC2/HIPAA evidence available.

- AWS region deprecation: Redwood's routing is policy-driven. If a region is deprecated we: (a) route new hosted requests to the next closest verified region by policy (latency/regulatory), (b) failover for active sessions depends on customer config — hosted customers can enable cross-region replication; Dedicated/Private customers remain isolated unless they opt into cross-region replication. For Private deployments, control plane changes are opt-in; customers retain control over VPC peering and KMS keys.

I'll loop in Karthik and Marissa to add specifics on Dedicated capacity and targeted remediation timelines.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Laura — quick internal summary so we can provide the level of detail MediSys expects. Points to confirm for the response doc:

1) Hosted behavior: we maintain region-to-region KV cache warming for frequently used prefixes; when a region is retired we proactively provision model variants in the target region and enable automatic reroute at the load balancer level. For eu customers we plan to migrate eu-central-legacy -> eu-west-3 as primary (timeline: Q4 2026) but we will keep a read-replica option in eu-north-1 during transition.

2) Dedicated customers: we offer a controlled migration plan — Reserved GPU pools are reprovisioned in the destination region; migration windows are scheduled; we guarantee final snapshot and KV cache export for customer-owned state.

3) Private (VPC/on-prem): control plane changes are opt-in. If a customer uses our Private control plane in their VPC, we can provide a maintenance window and a runbook; for air-gapped installs the customer manages the region shift.

4) Compliance artifacts: Marissa, please attach the latest subprocessor spreadsheet and the SOC2 evidence pointer. Neha, can you confirm whether we have any vendors that will not be available in eu-west-3 (so we can call those out)?

Thanks — I'll build a short non-technical impact statement for procurement and a technical annex for Security.

-Karthik
